newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sells 7.964 bln reais in Treasury papers.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sells 7.964 bln reais in Treasury papers.

text.p: Brazil's Central Bank, on behalf of the National Treasury, raised 7.964 billion reais in an auction of notes and letters, dealers said.
A total of 3.383 billion reais was sold in two series of National Treasury Letters known as LTNs.
A total of 3.061 billon reais of 183-day LTNs, due in December 1 1997, was sold at an overnight call money rate of 2.423 percent a month.
The Central Bank also sold 322 million reais of 365-day, due in June 1 1998, at a call money rate of 2.598 percent a month.
A total of 1.571 billion reais was sold in two series of dollar-indexed National Treasury notes (NTN-D).

The bank sold 1.055 billion reais of NTN-D notes, which are due on June 1 1999, and pay an annual yeld of 11.99 percent. The bank also sold 516 million reais of NTN-D notes coming due June 1 2000, paying an annual yield of 11.92 percent.

Some 3.010 billion reais were sold in National Treasury notes (NTN-H) indexed to the variation of Brazil's reference rate (TR). The notes, which are due in December 1 1997, pay annual yields of 13.06 percent plus the variation of the TR in the maturity period.
